summary: The candidate is a valid partial fix: it makes the DeepSeek-family CPU gate compute FP32 logits and rejects non-FP32 inputs at the Python CPU TopK boundary. It does not enforce the issue-wide router contract: ernie4.MoEGate still emits BF16 when its parameters are BF16, and the new TopK check converts that existing path into a ValueError. The optional specialized BF16-activation x FP32-weight AMX kernel also remains absent; FP32 DeepSeek router weights use the semantically correct unaccelerated fallback.

tests.what_was_measured: At the recorded base, forced DeepSeek AMX dispatch returned BF16 and biased_grouped_topk_cpu forwarded the identical BF16 tensor; FP32 logits 1.001 and 1.002 collapsed to a BF16 tie.
The candidate's five focused regressions passed at the exact candidate commit.

DeepSeek BF16 and FP32 weight branches returned FP32; BF16, FP16, and FP64 TopK inputs were rejected before mocked native dispatch; FP32 was forwarded unchanged. The installed native module did not expose biased_grouped_topk_cpu on this AMD host.
The actual ernie4.MoEGate returned torch.bfloat16 for BF16 input/weight, after which the candidate CPU TopK wrapper raised its FP32-contract ValueError.
On MI355X/gfx950, linear_bf16_fp32 returned FP32 for (7,9)x(11,9) and matched CPU FP32 matmul of the same BF16 operands with maximum absolute error 2.384185791015625e-07.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) executed the independent linear_bf16_fp32 numerical reference. This does not validate Intel AMX.

remaining_counterexamples: python/sglang/srt/models/ernie4.py MoEGate still uses F.linear(hidden_states, weight) without an FP32 conversion. With BF16 input and BF16 weight it emits BF16, and the candidate's biased_grouped_topk_cpu now raises ValueError instead of providing an FP32 router path.
The optional specialized BF16 activation x FP32 router-weight AMX kernel is not implemented; DeepSeek FP32 router weights remain on the semantically correct but unaccelerated FP32 F.linear fallback.
remaining_limitations: The host CPU is AMD EPYC 9575F and has no Intel AMX, so actual AMX packed-weight execution and performance were not validated.

The installed sgl_kernel module was /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sglang_kernel-0.4.6.post1-py3.12-linux-x86_64.egg/sgl_kernel/__init__.py and did not register biased_grouped_topk_cpu on this host, preventing direct native CPU TopK execution.
No native source changed in the candidate, so no native rebuild was applicable.
No affected full-model weights were available; no full-model, serving, semantic-accuracy, or distributed-workload claim is made.
